observation_summary: The operate method in both BigMatrixImpl and RealMatrixImpl throws an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when multiplying a non-square matrix by a vector, because the result vector is initialized with the length of the input vector instead of the number of rows in the matrix.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by an incorrect initialization of the result array. The code uses 'v.length' (the input vector's dimension) to size the output array, whereas the correct size for the result of a matrix-vector multiplication is the number of rows in the matrix ('nRows'). This is a classic case of an incorrect value being used for initialization, which is a direct fit for the Assignment/Initialization category.
evidence_used: BigMatrixImpl.java:991: final BigDecimal[] out = new BigDecimal[v.length];
RealMatrixImpl.java:779: final double[] out = new double[v.length];
Bug report description: 'The correct behaviour would of course be to create a vector with the same length as the row dimension of the matrix.'
Stack trace: java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 2 out of bounds for length 2

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic involves a calculation, the root cause is specifically the incorrect initialization of the output array size, not the mathematical procedure itself.
There is no missing guard or condition; the code simply uses the wrong variable to initialize the array size.
